chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Ya'qub ibn Yazid both of them, from Ibn Fuddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from al-Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say regarding the Word of the Mighty and Exalted:
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly.
He said: It is their affirmation of the Unity of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'willingly or unwillingly' mean in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that the universal submission mentioned in the verse refers specifically to the ontological acknowledgment of God’s oneness (*tawhid*), rather than ritual obedience. This interpretation highlights the distinction between the involuntary submission of all creation to Divine Will and the conscious faith of believers, a key theme in Shia theological discourse on the nature of *islam* versus *iman*.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. My Father (may Allah have mercy on him) that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim; ad Ya`qub ibn Yazid both of them on the authority of Ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Ibn Bukayr, on the authority of Zurarah that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to interpret the Word of the Mighty and High:
And to Him submits whoever is in heavens and the Earth, willingly or unwillingly.1
He said: “They are bound to the belief in the Unity of Allah, the Mighty and High.”
